title: sdk-docs-todo-scratchpad
body:
Daily scratchpad / SDK docs to-dos (notes to self)

2026-03-03
Quick log:
- Spent morning triaging feedback from community channel about JS SDK chaining and streaming examples.
- Ran through the TypeScript quickstart and hit two missing examples (function-calling + streaming chat).
- Noted perf confusion: users thinking streamed tokens are slower due to our example using small chunk size. Need to clarify.

Top priorities (next 7 days)
1) Quickstart refresh (high)
   - Update README to include streaming chat example (server and browser snippet).
   - Add explicit function-calling example showing request/response shapes and how to register types in TS.
   - Concrete code snippets for handling partial tokens + finalization.
   - Tests: add one e2e test that verifies stream emits messages and finalization event. (Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rdw-sdk/pull/482)

2) Sample apps (medium)
   - Minimal chat demo (Next.js) that showcases streaming + function calling + tool fallback.
     - UX notes: show partial tokens, provide cancel button, show model fallback if rate-limited.
   - Embeddings search example (Python + Node) with pagination and pagination token example.
   - TODO: pick 1 sample to ship in the repo README; others as separate examples/ folder.

3) Docs gaps to fill (medium-high)
   - Error handling patterns: show how to implement exponential backoff with jitter for rate limits and transient GPU OOMs.
   - Token counting examples: how to estimate/request tokens for cost/limits.
   - Batching recommendations for Redwood Dedicated customers (link to Optimize playbook).
   - Clarify caching behavior: prefix/KV caching examples and common mistakes.

4) TypeScript types + SDK ergonomics (low-medium)
   - Expose stronger generics for chat function responses so TS infers payload shapes (issue #418).
   - Add docs snippet showing how to type-check function calls and validate payload in runtime.

Notes / snippets to copy into docs
- Streaming chat (JS) minimal example:
  const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-chat-3b', messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'Explain coroutines in 2 sentences'}] });
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    // chunk.delta -> partial text
    // chunk.final -> final message object when done
  }

- Function calling (TS) snippet:
  type CreateUser = { name: string; email: string };
  const fn = client.registerFunction<CreateUser>('create_user', async (args) => {
    // validate args.name, args.email
    return { id: 'u_123' };
  });

Fragile/unknowns to follow up on
- Streaming chunk format: still some community confusion between chunk.delta vs chunk.content. Add a visual diagram in the quickstart.
- Clarify browser auth flow for private deployments (VPC customers): which headers are allowed, token rotation example. Sync with security team (Diego).
- Which models support function calling + streaming simultaneously? Add compatibility matrix.

Collaborator asks / handoffs
- @Alex: can you review the new TS type suggestions and help with the infer<> examples?
- @Diego: confirm recommended header patterns for browser + server usage for Private deploys; small write-up for quickstart.

Release checklist (for quickstart update)
- [ ] Update README.md + quickstart code blocks
- [ ] Add 1 integration test for streaming chat
- [ ] Merge PR and bump package docs site
- [ ] Publish short video demo (30-60s) for the sample chat app

Misc notes (scratch)
- Idea: sample app that compares latency/cost of streaming vs non-streaming for same prompt (graph, per-token cost). Could be a blog piece + sample.
- Keep language simple for PLG audience — engineers want copy-paste that works. Avoid too many infra caveats in quickstart; link to dedicated docs for deep dives.
- Leave TODO marker in the doc where we need a diagram: <<STREAMING-DIAGRAM>>

End of notes.

Unresolved questions to add to weekly sync:
- Do we want to include Redwood Optimize recommendations in quickstart or separate page? (Pros: helps default configs; Cons: too much for first-run UX)
- Should sample apps live in examples/ or a new "tutorials/" repo?
__notes_for_indexing: personal scratchpad: informal, choppy phrases, todos, linked GH issues and PRs
